newsitem.title: UK: BBC Finance Director to step down.
newsitem.headline: BBC Finance Director to step down.

text.p: Rodney Baker-Bates, BBC Director of Finance and Information Technology, plans to leave the corporation when his contract expires next March, the BBC said on Friday.
Deputy Finance Director John Smith will take over the financial role while the technology job will be separated out and an appointment made in due course.
Baker-Bates, who worked for Midland Bank before joining the BBC in 1993, is credited with helping to turn around the corporation's finances.
The BBC said this month it had a positive cash balance of 365 million stg after wiping put borrowings which peaked at 183 million in 1993/94.

BBC Director-General John Birt said Baker-Bates had played "the critical role" in that success. "At the same time he has enabled the BBC to understand the vital role which computer technology will play in everything we do in the future," Birt added in a statement.
Smith joined the BBC's corporate finance department in 1989 and has been in his current job for 18 months.
A BBC spokeswoman said Baker-Bates, 52 this year, plans to go into semi-retirement but will continue to hold a number of non-executive directorships.
